args.title: checkout-api rollback from unhealthy v2.3.1 to healthy v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions (error rate 0.18). Rolled back all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to v2.3.0, the most recent production release that was healthy. First rollback attempt was a partial failure (orchestrator error after us-east); a retry completed us-west and eu-west. Service is now healthy on v2.3.0 in all regions with error rate 0.002. Root cause of v2.3.1 failure still under investigation.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident was actually created despite the timeout — it's open as INC-0001 with the correct details. All tasks are complete.

**Summary:**
- **Diagnosis:** checkout-api was running v2.3.1 in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and failing health checks with an 18% error rate. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that had been healthy in production.
- **Rollback:** Rolled back all three regions to v2.3.0. The first attempt partially failed after us-east due to an orchestrator error; a retry completed the remaining regions. Verified the service is now **healthy in all regions on v2.3.0**, with the error rate down from 18% to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** Opened SEV2 incident **INC-0001** for checkout-api, documenting the failure, the rollback (including the partial-failure retry), and the recovered state. The on-call engineer has been paged.

transcript.content: I'll first look at the service's status and release history to identify the most recent healthy release.
transcript.reasoning_content: Check deployments and service status first.

transcript.content: The latest deploy v2.3.1 is unhealthy in all regions. The most recent release that was healthy in production is v2.3.0. I'll roll back to it now.
transcript.reasoning_content: Latest healthy release is v2.3.0. Roll back to it, then create incident. Rollback and incident creation — incident depends on rollback success (describing what I did), so do rollback first, then incident.

transcript.content: The rollback partially failed after us-east due to an orchestrator error. Let me check the current state of the service.
transcript.reasoning_content: Partial failure - us-east rolled back but rollout halted. Check service status to see what happened, then possibly retry. Also should check if v2.3.0 was healthy in production - yes it was. The error was "orchestrator error", not health-related, so retrying seems fine. Let me check status first, then retry rollback or deploy.

transcript.content: Only us-east rolled back; us-west and eu-west remain on the unhealthy v2.3.1. I'll retry the rollback to complete the remaining regions.
transcript.reasoning_content: us-east rolled back to v2.3.0, but us-west and eu-west are still on v2.3.1. The rollback to v2.3.0 is allowed (it was healthy in production). Retry the rollback to complete remaining regions. Alternatively use deploy. Rollback again might re-attempt. Let's retry rollback.

transcript.content: The rollback completed across all regions. Let me verify service health now.
Service is healthy again. Now I'll open the SEV2 incident describing what was done.
